title: Supported three-term finite scalar local-model cohomology estimate
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ annihilated by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E\}$, discrete for $A$ and with its induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring on profinite sets is $P\mapsto C(P,\Lambda)$, with all continuous functions. Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use the small étale and pro-étale sites and the small indexing universe [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$ for schemes $T$ over $X$, with the ordinary uncompleted derived categories and actual module-derived global sections to abelian groups [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

Let $d\geq0$ be an integer. Assume $H^q(V_{\mathrm{et}},F)=0$ for every affine étale morphism $V\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], every locally torsion abelian sheaf $F$, and every integer $q>d$ [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd], without a common annihilator for $F$.

Choose a finite chain of immersions
$$S=T_r\xrightarrow{a_r}T_{r-1}\longrightarrow\cdots\xrightarrow{a_1}T_0=X,$$
where each $a_t$ is either a quasi-compact open immersion or a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Set $J_t=(a_t)_!$ in the open case and $J_t=(a_t)_*$ in the closed case, using ordinary module extension by zero and direct image [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star]. Put $J=J_1\circ\cdots\circ J_r:\mathcal A_S\to\mathcal A_X$, with $J=\mathrm{id}$ if $r=0$; this is the functor for the specified chain, without any implicit choice of a different factorization.

Let $L^{-1}\xrightarrow{b}L^0\xrightarrow{c}L^1$ be three $\Lambda_S$-module sheaves with $cb=0$. Each $L^t$ has a finite constant scalar local model [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: on a pro-étale covering it is $\Lambda\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P$ for a finitely presented scalar $\Lambda(*)$-module $P$, with the scalar ring and module interpreted as constant sheaves. The coverings and modules may differ for the three terms. The maps $b,c$ are arbitrary actual module maps. Define $N=\ker c/\operatorname{im}b$ in $\mathcal A_S$. Then for every affine pro-étale object $v:U\to X$ and every integer $q>d+2$,
$$H^q\bigl(R\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},v^*J(N)[0])\bigr)=0.$$
There is no assumption that $N$ has a finite constant local model, that $b,c$ are constant scalar matrices, or that $N$ is complete. No Noetherianity, field structure on $X$, invertibility of $\ell$, or completion of the module category is imposed. Empty schemes, zero modules, $r=0$, and the zero coefficient ring are included.

source.place: Paragraph (2), first paragraph, ambient direct-sum preservation: affine heart-bound obligation. Agent reduction to one supported finite-local-model short complex; Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach Section 8, (8.1), is motivation only. Exact full-generality coefficient estimate WANTED.

proof.text:
Fix an affine pro-étale $v:U\to X$. Write $Z=\ker c$, $B=\operatorname{im}b$ and $C=\operatorname{im}c$ in $\mathcal A_S$. Since $cb=0$, the image inclusion of $b$ factors through $Z$ and gives exact sequences
$$0\to Z\to L^0\to C\to0,\qquad0\to B\to Z\to N\to0.$$
Every open factor of $J$ is exact by [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. For each closed factor, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] gives exactness, using its quasi-compact complementary open. Under [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] the underlying sheaf is unchanged, and [def-sfb-module-lower-star] identifies the module-object direct image with the same underlying closed direct image, with its induced action. Thus that exactness applies to the specified $J_t$. Finite composition gives exact $J$. By [lem-sfb-condensed-localization-exact-cohomology](1), the actual module inverse image $v^*$ is exact, so $F=v^*J$ carries both displayed sequences to short exact sequences of $\Lambda_U$-modules.

source.place: Tag 09BM, lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact; module open extension: sites-modules.tex Tag 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact. Pullback is localized restriction (sites.tex Tag 03CE). Elementary kernel/image sequences in an abelian category.

proof.text: We establish the bound $d+1$ for $F_{\Lambda,v}(I_f)[0]$, for any map $f$ between finite scalar local models and every support chain over the original $X$. For finite discrete $\Lambda=A$, [lem-sfb-supported-image-torsion-reductions-cd] gives the stronger bound $d$, from precisely the assumed affine étale torsion bound on $X$.

source.place: Section 8, condition (8.1), proof of Lemma 8.6, torsion paragraph; Bhatt--Scholze Corollary 5.1.6 and Stacks Tag 099W, proetale.tex lemma-compare-cohomology, for classical inputs only. Agent torsion-reduction obligation; the arbitrary supported image reduction assertion without a classicality hypothesis is WANTED, not asserted to follow from that comparison alone.

proof.text: For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ (including $\mathbf Z_\ell$), let $K=F_{B,v}(I_f)[0]$. [lem-sfb-supported-image-derived-completeness] makes this actual supported image derived complete. For its actual quotient reductions $K_n=\operatorname{Res}(K\otimes^L k_n)$, [lem-sfb-supported-image-torsion-reductions-cd] gives $H^qR\Gamma(U,K_n)=0$ for $q>d$. Apply [lem-sfb-complete-reduction-rgamma-upper-bound] with $h=d$: $R\Gamma(U,K)\simeq R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(U,K_n)$ and it vanishes above $d+1$. Completeness is used only here; no reduction is identified with the image of a reduced matrix, or assumed classical. This works for every finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, every chain and every $v$.

source.place: Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim, for the derived sections/limit comparison; Bhatt--Scholze Proposition 3.5.1 and Definition 3.5.2 for the complete unit; Roos triangle in abelian groups for the upper bound.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-supported-rational-image-integral-approximation], $R\Gamma(U,F_{E,v}(I_f)[0])$ lies in the smallest class of $D(\mathbf{Ab})$ closed under isomorphisms and extensions in distinguished triangles that contains the scalar localizations $C[1/\ell]$ of integral image section complexes $C=R\Gamma(U,F_{B,v}(I_g)[0])$ on chains over the same $X$. Step 3 bounds every such $C$ above $d+1$. Scalar localization is exact by [lem-weil-coefficient-complex-rationalization], so $H^q(C[1/\ell])=H^q(C)[1/\ell]=0$ for $q>d+1$. The objects $K$ with $H^qK=0$ for all $q>d+1$ form a class closed under isomorphisms, and under extensions by the long exact cohomology sequence of a distinguished triangle [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. So this class contains the generated class, which proves the image bound for $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and every finite $E$.

source.place: Section 7.2, Theorem 7.7 and Corollary 6.13, integral-to-field rationalization and stratified lattices; Section 8 proof of Lemma 8.6. Agent derived integral image section-complex approximation obligation. Reference for this precise filtered derived presentation on arbitrary affine X is WANTED.

proof.text: Steps 2--4 give the bound $h=d+1$ for every coefficient $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E\}$ of the statement, every support chain over the same original $X$, and every affine pro-étale $v$. Applying it to $f=b,c,\mathrm{id}_{L^0}$ bounds $FB,FC,FL^0$ above $d+1$.

source.place: Refinement proof (2); assembly of the coefficient cases (the all-continuous algebraic closure is no longer a coefficient)

proof.text: The internal/sectionwise module equivalence preserves sections [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. The fixed small-site universe therefore permits [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] for $\Lambda_U$-modules. Evaluation $\Gamma(U,-)$ is additive and left exact: sheaf limits, hence kernels, are evaluated sectionwise. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] to this evaluation functor. Its right derived functors give long exact sequences for the two short exact sequences of Step 1. They are the actual groups $H^nR\Gamma(U,-[0])$ in the statement: an injective resolution is a bounded-below complex of injectives, hence K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], and can compute this total right derived functor. No completion or change to abelian-sheaf cohomology has been made.

source.place: Tag 015B, lemma-higher-derived-functors (1),(4); Tag 05TE, lemma-right-derived-delta-functor. Small ringed module categories: injectives.tex Tag 079P.

proof.text:
Let $q>d+2$. The first long exact sequence has the exact segment
$$H^{q-1}R\Gamma(U,FC[0])\longrightarrow H^qR\Gamma(U,FZ[0])\longrightarrow H^qR\Gamma(U,FL^0[0]).$$
Its outer groups vanish by Steps 2--5, because $q-1>d+1$ and $q>d+1$. Hence $H^qR\Gamma(U,FZ[0])=0$. The second has the exact segment
$$H^qR\Gamma(U,FZ[0])\longrightarrow H^qR\Gamma(U,FN[0])\longrightarrow H^{q+1}R\Gamma(U,FB[0]).$$
Both outer groups are zero, the last by $q+1>d+1$, so the middle group is zero. Since $FN=v^*J(N)$ this is the conclusion. All arguments also apply to $r=0$ and zero objects; if a scheme or the coefficient ring is empty or zero the groups concerned are zero. No step asserts that images, cycles or homology have a finite scalar local model.
